paragraphs.text: sc. Of Engedi, 1Sa 24:1 Loquitur in spelunca, sed prophetat in Christo, saith Hilary.
paragraphs.anchor: When he was in the cave

paragraphs.text: sc. Of my heart, and more with my mind than mouth; for if he had been heard, he had been taken up by the enemy. Thus Moses cried, but uttered nothing, Exo 14:15, Egit vocis silentio, ut corde clamaret (Aug.). Thus Christ cried, Heb 5:7.
paragraphs.anchor: I cried unto the Lord with my voice

paragraphs.text: Plainly and plentifully, how my danger increased to a very crisis, as one expresseth it.
Or, covered over, with grief, as the Greek expoundeth it.
paragraphs.anchor: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me

paragraphs.text: sc. That I neither fretted nor fainted; or, thou knewest how to make a way to escape, 1Co 10:13. The Lord knoweth how to deliver his, 2Pe 2:9.
Not a man would appear for me. Aφιλον το δυστυχες, misery is friendless for the most part. See 2Ti 4:16. Nulla fides unquam miseros delegit amicos.
paragraphs.anchor: I looked on my right hand

paragraphs.text: I ran to thee, as my last refuge, in the fail of all outward comforts. Zep 3:12, they are an "afflicted poor people"; and being so, "they trust in the name of the Lord."
paragraphs.anchor: I cried unto thee, O Lord

paragraphs.text: Exhausted and drawn dry; utterly wasted, and disabled to help myself any way, Depauperatus sum (Vat.).
paragraphs.anchor: For I am brought very low

paragraphs.text: i.e. Out of this distress, wherewith I am no less straitened than if in prison.
paragraphs.anchor: Bring my soul out of prison

paragraphs.text: Heb. shall crown me; that is, shall encircle me, as wondering at thy goodness in my deliverance; or they shall set the crown on mine head, as the saints do likewise upon Christ’s head, {Son 3:11} to whom this psalm may be fitly applied all along, as above said.
paragraphs.anchor: The righteous shall compass me about
